welcome.title: Welcome to Octa Pass
welcome.subtitle: Free, open source and end-to-end encrypted.
welcome.localHelp: No account: your vault stays in this browser. You can turn on sync later.

local.name: This device
local.createSubtitle: Your vault is encrypted with your master password and stays in this browser. Nothing is sent anywhere.
local.guidance: There’s no account to reset it from, so use a long passphrase you’ll remember. There is no recovery beyond your backups: back up your vault so a broken laptop doesn’t take it with it.
local.creating: Encrypting… this takes a few seconds
local.weak: Choose a stronger master password. Four or more random words work well.
local.kitTitle: Write down your backup recovery code
local.kitSubtitle: If you forget your master password, this code opens your backups. Nobody else has a copy.
local.kitConfirm: I’ve written it down somewhere safe
local.restoreSubtitle: Open an .octapass-backup file as this browser’s vault.
local.restoreFailed: That file, password or code didn’t open a backup. Check them and try again.
local.sectionHelp: Your vault is only in this browser. Back it up, or turn on sync to use it everywhere.
local.backUpHelp: Downloads an encrypted .octapass-backup file. Keep it somewhere other than this computer.
local.reminder_one: Last backup {count} day ago. Back up your vault so you don’t lose it with this browser.
local.reminder_other: Last backup {count} days ago. Back up your vault so you don’t lose it with this browser.
local.reminderNever: Your vault isn’t backed up yet. Back it up so you don’t lose it with this browser.
local.showCodeHelp: Opens your backups if you forget your master password.
local.turnOnSyncHelp: Creates an account and moves this vault into it, encrypted as it is, so it syncs to your other devices.
local.syncSubtitle: Create an account and move this vault into it. Everything stays encrypted on the way.
local.syncDoneSubtitle: Your vault is in your new account now, and on this device as before.
local.needsApp: This vault is bound to this computer’s security chip through the Octa Pass app. Open the app, then try again.
local.chipBoundHelp: The Octa Pass app’s security chip protects this vault too, so a copy of it is useless elsewhere. It needs the app to open. If the app or this computer goes, your backups bring it back.

browser.title: Browser’s password manager
browser.useOctaPass: Use Octa Pass instead of {browser}’s password manager
browser.useOctaPassHelp: {browser} stops offering to save and fill what Octa Pass does. Turn this off to get its offers back.
browser.denied: Octa Pass needs permission to change {browser}’s privacy settings to do this.
browser.firefoxForms: Firefox doesn’t let extensions turn off its address and card autofill. Turn them off in Firefox’s settings, under Privacy & Security.
browser.safari: Safari doesn’t let extensions change this. On a Mac, open Safari › Settings › AutoFill. On iPhone or iPad, open Settings › Apps › Safari › AutoFill. Turn off what you want Octa Pass to do instead.
browser.offerTitle: Use Octa Pass instead of {browser}’s password manager?
browser.offerBody: Then only Octa Pass offers to save and fill passwords, addresses and cards.

fillOnLoad.title: Filling
fillOnLoad.label: Fill logins when a page opens
fillOnLoad.help: On a sign-in page, Octa Pass fills the login you used last on that site without waiting for you to pick it. Only on secure (https) pages, only with logins saved for that exact address, and never when Octa Pass would ask you to confirm it’s you first. Start typing to replace what was filled. The website can read what’s filled, as it can after any fill.

apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.offerHelp: When you paste what looks like an API key into a website, Octa Pass asks whether to save it. It’s recognised on this device, and the key is only used if you choose Save.

neverSave.title: Never offered to save
neverSave.help: Sites where you answered “Never for this site”.
